info.description:
Bodies of HTTP requests and responses, where applicable, are JSON structures. The encoding used may be UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32. Where time stamps are used, they are encoded using [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601); the time zone used is UTC.

The TCP port to be used for the HTTP requests is configuration-dependent; by default, it is 55300.

By default, a client first needs to log in and acquire a session via [/login](#/Authentication/login) before accessing any other endpoints.
info.title: openTCS Kernel Web API v8 (preview, 7.4.0)

tags.description:
The following endpoints do not specify actual web API endpoints, but rather messages published by the openTCS kernel using the Server-Sent Events (SSE) technology. The openTCS kernel exclusively uses named events to send messages to connected clients. Each endpoint represents a named event and starts with a `/sse::` prefix, followed by the name of the corresponding event. As an example, the `/sse::/events/vehicles` endpoint represents the named event `/events/vehicles`. The response body of an endpoint specifies the data contained in the respective named event.

To avoid redundant documentation, descriptions for the properties in the response body schemas are omitted. Instead, refer to the API documentation of the corresponding Java classes for detailed information on the semantics of the properties.
tags.name: Server-Sent Events - Named Events

UserPermission.description:
Possible user permission values:
* `READ_DATA` - Indicates the user may retrieve any data from the kernel.
* `SHUTDOWN_KERNEL` - Indicates the user may shut down the kernel.
* `LOAD_MODEL` - Indicates the user may load another model.
* `LOCK_RESOURCE` - Indicates the user may add or remove temporary locks at paths or locations.
* `UPDATE_ROUTING_TOPOLOGY` - Indicates the user may update the routing topology.
* `MODIFY_VEHICLE` - Indicates the user may move/place vehicles and modify their states.
* `MODIFY_ORDER` - Indicates the user may create/modify transport orders.
* `MODIFY_ORDER_SEQUENCE` - Indicates the user may create/modify order sequences.
* `MODIFY_PERIPHERAL` - Indicates the user may modify peripheral states.
* `MODIFY_PERIPHERAL_JOB` - Indicates the user may create/modify peripheral jobs.

incompleteName.description: Whether the name of the transport order is considered to be incomplete. If set, the kernel will complete the name according to its configuration, e.g. by appending a suffix to it. It is recommended to set this, as names generated by the kernel can be guaranteed to be unique, while clients typically cannot guarantee this.

type.description: The (optional) type of the transport order
